title: Desk-to-desk link: pair two desks for their teammates, with a durable, revocable link channel

title: Cross-desk messaging: message_teammate, threads and replies over the link, under the recipient's grants
summary: - 2026-10-13T07:31:38.577Z: [claude] On dispatch/epic-3: an ask or handoff to a linked teammate waits in the sender's exchange_pair, crosses when the queue takes it up, and runs on the recipient desk under that desk's allowedSenders (by qualified id) and a card on the recipient's tape; the sender's desk can't answer the card. The result returns over the link, kept until it arrives, and each desk keeps its own copy of the pair thread. Unlinking fails pending messages with "X is on D, which isn't linked any more.", withdraws cards and ends grants, and a stop on the recipient's desk answers the sender. Tests cover ask, handoff, reply, offline both ways, deny, revoke, ambiguity and bounds. Not done: the sender does not see a "waiting for the person" state while the other desk's card is open (residual in the ADR).

title: Linked desks: teammates on different desks collaborate as if they shared one room

ADR 0003 records it. UI: one rail across desks with a desk filter.

title: Desk: front-to-teammate bridge
summary: Front tools: send_to_teammate(words) passes the person's own words, unrephrased, into the teammate's session as start-or-steer in its open chapter (same path, grants and chapter as a typed message; voice origin kept); remain_silent. Teammate side: start/end fragments like Codex's realtime_start/end ('behind an intermediary; input is a transcript and may have recognition errors'; 'call ended, resume normal behaviour'). Back to the front: short progress notes while the turn runs, the reply's <spoken> line spoken verbatim (inject as text the front must say, or client-side speech), approvals/questions become 'it needs you to approve on the desk/phone'. A second send while a turn runs steers it. Front never reports work the teammate did not.

title: Desk: GPT-Live front over the ChatGPT login
summary: Built 2026-10-15 on release/0.38.0 (618a827a), pending George's QA. voice/realtime/live.rs places the call as the Codex app does: POST chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls?intent=quicksilver&architecture=avas with the ChatGPT login's bearer + ChatGPT-Account-ID, openai-alpha quicksilver=v2, JSON {sdp, session{model gpt-live-1-codex, instructions, audio.output.voice, delegation{type client}}}; call id from Location; sideband wss://api.openai.com/v1/live/<call id>. The desk (not the phone) is the WebRTC peer (webrtc 0.20.3 + opus 0.4, as Codex pins): mic PCM 24k doubled to 48k, Opus 20 ms packets paced with silence fill; host candidates only. The sideband carries speech as 24 kHz PCM (session.output_audio.delta), transcripts, turns and delegation.created, so no Opus decode. delegation.created -> the bridge's send_to_teammate; a line to say -> session.context.append speakable (said in the model's own words, not verbatim); person's turn -> barge-in. Lines wait for session.started; create retried on 5xx/unreachable; sideband rejoined; ended call or failed peer drops the front to the pipeline. Free against the Voice budget. Voices: cove (default), juniper, maple, spruce, ember, vale, breeze, sol. Settings: Live calls > Model > OpenAI > GPT-Live (Included with your ChatGPT subscription). Proof: live/tests.rs unit tests + ignored live test (HOTLINE_TEST_CHATGPT_DIR, HOTLINE_TEST_ASK_WAV) passed 3/3 against the real service; make check green. Build needs cmake (docs/development.md). Not done: 60-minute session renewal (falls back to pipeline), attestation header (not required today).
constraints: Private route: behind a feature flag, fails soft to Grok or the pipeline
